headline: Approved a Where Do We Stand art installation on Essex Street, pending artist talks, and outreach to six sculptures for loan.
summary: Members accepted a donated model of the former Salem train station for display in City Hall Annex. Staff also reported on Artists' Row tenants, a Rousseau gift headed to City Council in November, and about $11,000 in unallocated sculpture funds. Ideas for painted fire call boxes were discussed, but no vote was taken.
decisions: Approved the August 18, 2026 minutes, with Mr. Apito abstaining.
Approved the Where Do We Stand proposal by Mark Sheridan for Essex Street, contingent on further discussion with the artist; passed with all present voting yes.
Accepted the gift of a model of the former Salem train station for display at City Hall Annex, unanimously.
Approved approaching the six highest-ranked sculptures for the loan program, using the existing budget, unanimously.

decision_titles: Where Do We Stand public art installation on Essex Street
Train station model gift of art
Six sculptures for the Sculpture Garden Loan Program
plain_text:
MEETING MINUTES 
Note: All proposals, presentations, and/or documentation to be reviewed and 
discussed at this meeting can be viewed online at the following link: 
https://bit.ly/SalemPACProposals 
Meeting called to order at 6:33pm. 
Roll Call PAC: Jim Bostick (Chair), Becky Fisher, Gwendolyn Rosemond, Brittany Minton, 
Bryan Apito, Joseph “Joe” Badowski. 
Absent at Roll Call: Hannah Gathman. 
Also Present: Staff: Julie Barry (Senior Planner Arts & Culture); Maura Welch (Clerk). 
The Commission welcomed new member Joseph Badowski, and members introduced 
themselves. 
• Meeting Minutes Approval - August 18, 2026 Meeting Minutes 
The Commission reviewed the August 18, 2026 meeting minutes. No corrections were 
raised. Mr. Apito abstained because he had not attended the August meeting. Joseph was 
identified as a new member and did not vote on the minutes. 
Motion to approve the August 18, 2026 minutes is made by Ms. Fisher, Ms. Rosemond 
seconds, with all present approving with the exception of Mr. Apito who abstains. The chair 
stated that the minutes were approved. 
• Artists’ Row Tenant Updates 
Ms. Barry reported that the recommended tenants for Stall #1 accepted the offer to share 
the space and have met to plan how to display their work and share responsibility for 
keeping the space open. North Shore Glass School and MiraMar Printmakers also accepted 
continued tenancy in Stalls #2 and #4, respectively. Both the 2027 and 2028 Public Artist in 
Residence offers were accepted, and contracts are in progress.

Ms. Barry said the necessary legal approvals and documentation for the taxidermy work had 
been obtained. A group meeting with the Artists’ Row support network is planned for the 
following month. 
• Rousseau Collection Gift of Art 
Ms. Barry reported that the gift documentation had been approved by procurement and 
legal and was being circulated for signatures. The paperwork was also being prepared for 
City Council consideration, anticipated in November. She thanked Ms. Minton for her work 
on the arrangements. 
Mr. Bostick is photographing the framed works. Ms. Barry will coordinate installation with 
the Facilities Department and share the installation guidance, including the 
recommendation to use two anchor points and D-rings. 
• Where Do We Stand Public Art Proposal 
Ms. Barry presented a proposal by Mark Sheridan for a four-hour interactive public art 
installation on the Essex Street pedestrian mall on a weekend in November. The proposed 
display would invite passersby to respond to questions and engage in conversation. The 
proposal stated that no recordings would be made and the materials would be removed 
after the event. 
Members expressed interest in the concept and asked for further clarification about the 
artist’s goals, approach, and potential impact on the public. Several members had not yet 
watched the artist’s TED talk. Ms. Barry offered to speak further with the artist and invite 
individual feedback from members who reviewed the video. 
Motion to approve the proposal contingent on Ms. Barry’s further discussion with the artist, 
with discretion to decline if the approach presents concerns for the public, is made by Ms. 
Fisher, seconded by Mr. Apito, with all present voting yes. The chair stated that the motion 
passed. 
• Train Station Model Gift of Art 
Ms. Barry presented a proposed gift of a handmade model of the former Salem train 
station, created by Leon Massey using recycled materials. The family proposed donating the 
model to the City and wished it to remain on display. A location on the first floor of the City 
Hall Annex was identified, and the family would provide a display case and specially made 
table. 
Ms. Barry reported that the stated replacement value was approximately $950, so the gift 
would not require City Council approval under the process discussed. She will prepare gift 
documentation and circulate it for signatures. 
Motion to accept the gift and display it at the location described is made by Mr. Apito moves 
to approve, Ms. Rosemond moves to second, and it passes unanimously. The chair stated 
that the motion passed.
• 400+ Sculpture Project and FY2027 Budget Update 
Ms. Barry reported that Roark Congdon attended the sculpture dedication and received the 
previously approved $2,000 travel stipend. The Harbor Master had asked whether the 
Commission wanted a concrete or granite footing around the sculpture’s base. Members 
did not feel it was necessary, noting the industrial character of the piece and the possibility 
of a future relocation. 
Ms. Barry reviewed signage quotes and the updated budget. A local woman-owned sign 
business quoted approximately $500 including installation for a comparable sign, while 
another quote was approximately $1,700 plus installation. Members supported Ms. Barry 
confirming the materials and proceeding with the lower-cost local vendor if she was 
satisfied with the quality. No formal vote was taken. 
Installation savings and updated estimates left approximately $11,000 in unallocated funds. 
Members discussed potential uses, including public art mini grants, ArtBox projects, the 
Salem Arts Festival community art project, and additional sculptures on loan. Members 
noted that decisions about programs requiring calls for artists should be made in time for 
possible January calls. FY2027 funds must be spent by June 30, 2027. 
• South Harbor Garage Window Art 
Ms. Barry presented proposed replacement window banners by current Public Artist in 
Residence Erin Survilas. The Women of Salem concept uses a vintage newspaper format and 
portraits of three women connected with Salem. The design was funded through the Artists’ 
Row budget; the estimated cost to print the three banners is $432. 
Members supported the concept and portraits and suggested refining the typography, scale 
and balance so that the women and their portraits are more prominent. Mr. Bostick offered 
to work with the artist on feedback. Ms. Barry will share the discussion with the artist and 
bring revised designs back to the Commission before printing. No funding vote was taken. 
• Decommissioned Fire Call Boxes 
Ms. Barry reported that the City Electrical Department had asked whether the Commission 
would consider artwork on decommissioned fire call boxes that remain on street corners. 
An initial list identified 22 downtown locations; four boxes were marked as particularly 
historic. Approximately 100 boxes may exist across the city, though the total and future 
plans require confirmation. 
Members discussed preserving the historic boxes, commissioning artists to paint others, 
and exploring whether a limited number of surplus boxes could be sold to support public 
art. They also discussed identifying the boxes as nonfunctioning so that the public would 
not mistake them for active emergency call boxes. A small pilot and a future call for artists 
were suggested. 
Ms. Barry will ask the Electrical Department about the number of boxes, planned removals, 
the future of painted boxes, and whether any can be sold. She will consult appropriate City
staff about historic preservation and the legal and financial requirements for fundraising. 
She offered to prepare a draft call for artists for a future meeting. No vote or allocation was 
made. 
• Sculpture Garden Loan Program 
Ms. Barry reported on a visit to the Flying Horse Sculpture Exhibition at Pingree with curator 
Judith Klein and Commission members. Ms. Fisher compiled a poll to help members rank 
potential works. The Commission reviewed images and poll results, discussed the possibility 
of adding works beyond the six already budgeted, and considered transportation, 
installation, stipend and procurement issues. 
The six leading works were identified as works by Thomas Berger, Barbara Galazzo, Josie 
Campbell Dellenbaugh, Jose Criollo, Morris Norvin and Gary Rathmell. Ms. Barry will work with 
Ms. Klein to approach the artists and report on availability. If a work is unavailable, the 
next-ranked backup may be considered within the existing budget. 
Ms. Barry will also discuss with Ms. Klein the possibility of asking artists for loan rates in 
future years and consult the City procurement team as appropriate. The Commission did 
not approve an increased budget or a seventh sculpture at this meeting. 
Motion to approach the six highest-ranked works, using the existing budget and the ranked 
backups as needed, is made by Ms. Fisher, seconded by Ms. Minton, and passes 
unanimously. 
• Budget Check-In and Adjournment 
Members requested a brief standing budget check-in at future meetings, with an updated 
budget available in the meeting documents. Ms. Barry agreed to add the item, likely at the 
end of the agenda. 
Motion to adjourn is made by Mr. Badowski, seconded by Ms. Fisher, and all those in 
attendance vote yes.   
Adjourn - The meeting adjourned at 8:21pm.
